rationale: The differential validation shows golden_rejected: the golden submission fails SR1 with an internally contradictory message ('fault-injection target (sig_p_reg) is inconsistent with vulnerable_register's primary register (sig_q_reg)') even though both are sig_p_reg. The evaluator's own internal self-check also logs a MISMATCH (expected=sig_p_reg, got target=None, ambiguous=True) at startup, confirming the bug is in evaluate.py's extraction logic (determine_trigger_fault_target()/extract_fault_targets()), not in the golden answer, which correctly and consistently names sig_p_reg throughout. Because the golden cannot pass, mutation_score is not meaningful (blocked_by_differential) and discrimination coverage is 0.0 despite mapping coverage of 1.0. This is a pure evaluator regex/parsing defect, so evaluation_framework must be revised.
revision_instructions: In evaluate.py, the SR1 check (trigger-fault-target vs vulnerable_register consistency check) has a text-extraction bug: it must be rewritten to reliably parse which register name is called out as the *fault target* within the trigger_scenario free-text field, regardless of sentence structure (e.g., register name and its baseline/correct value mentioned in the same sentence, fault verb before or after the register mention, or use of pronouns referring back to the register). The current regex/clause-boundary approach returns ambiguous=True or None when both a register name and its correct baseline value appear together in one sentence, and produces a contradictory diagnostic where the same register name is reported as both the fault target and as inconsistent with itself. Do not require any particular sentence phrasing or keyword ordering — instead, require only that the trigger_scenario text names exactly one of the two valid branch register identifiers (as introduced/defined in the pinned interface) as being forced/faulted/corrupted, extract that occurrence robustly (e.g., by finding all mentions of the two valid register names anywhere in the trigger_scenario text alongside nearby fault-indicating verbs such as force/flip/corrupt/perturb, and picking the register most closely associated with such a verb rather than assuming a fixed clause pattern), and compare it against the primary register named in the vulnerable_register field for equality. Add the golden's own trigger_scenario as one of the regression self-check fixtures (already partially present) and make the self-check assertion fail the evaluate.py run loudly at startup (not just log a diagnostic MISMATCH) whenever extraction disagrees with the expected register, so this class of bug cannot ship silently again. After the fix, re-run the differential: the golden submission must pass SR1 (and all other requirements) while the naive baseline must continue to fail everything, and mutation scoring must then become meaningful.
